# Zod implementation-owner holdout v2

Evaluator: `353ebfebf863acd9aa922783fd3b29a724a66bfc34f281b3ee3894ee9a4d407a`

## Decisions

- Single automatic hint: **reject**
- Top-five hypothesis shortlist: **reject**

Exact delivered precision: 5/11; top-five recall: 10/20; discovery top-five recall: 3/9.

## Interpretation

The time-forward result rejects both lexical steering variants. Exact matches
work when issue language and implementation declarations share a distinctive
name (`$ZodFunction`, `recordProcessor`, `datetime`). They fail when the actual
fix belongs to an unnamed helper (`finalizeIssue`, `convertBaseSchema`,
`codePointLength`) or spans several cooperating surfaces. High confidence does
not solve this: plausible public facades and adjacent concepts also receive
large margins.

Keep both owner rankers diagnostic-only and do not disclose either a single
implementation owner or a top-five list to an agent. The next mechanism must be
evidence-conditioned: run a red probe first, collect a runtime trace/coverage
slice or a static compiler/import slice, and select an owner only when observed
execution or dependency evidence intersects the lexical candidates. Test that
on a new time-forward corpus; neither v1 nor v2 can serve as held-out evidence
again.
